items.name: ab-test-results
items.title: A/B Test Results
items.description: Variants with lift, a confidence interval and a two-proportion z-test — plus the peeking warning, because stopping at the first significant reading is the failure that actually happens.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: A stack of collapsible sections. Each header is a real button inside a heading, which is what makes the set navigable by heading in a screen reader.

items.name: address-input
items.title: Address Input
items.description: A postal address whose shape follows the country. A US form asks for a State and a ZIP; a UK one asks for a County and a Postcode; Japan puts the postal code first. Shipping the US layout everywhere is how forms reject valid addresses.

items.name: agent-card
items.title: Agent Card
items.description: One agent’s definition as a card: the model behind it, the tools it may reach for, and whether it is allowed to run. Tools are listed by name rather than counted, because a count tells you nothing about blast radius.

items.name: agent-memory
items.title: Agent Memory
items.description: What an agent has remembered and where each piece came from. Distinct from retrieval: these are injected into every future run whether relevant or not, which is why a person has to be able to inspect and delete them.

items.name: agent-steps
items.title: Agent Steps
items.description: An agent's plan with each step's state. The whole plan is shown from the start, including steps not yet reached — revealing them one at a time hides how much is left, which is what someone watching most wants to know.

items.name: agent-tasks
items.title: Agent Tasks
items.description: The plan an agent is working from, as it works through it. Not a trace of what happened — a list of what it intends to do, which is what lets you see it heading somewhere wrong while there is still time to stop it.

items.name: alert-dialog
items.title: Alert Dialog
items.description: A modal that interrupts to confirm something consequential. Unlike Dialog it has no backdrop dismissal and no corner close — a destructive confirmation should take a deliberate answer.

items.name: alert-triage
items.title: Alert Triage
items.description: An alert queue grouped by fingerprint. A flapping check fires two hundred times, and an ungrouped list buries every other alert underneath it — which is how real pages get missed.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: A prominent message that stays on the page. Keeps the colour system, and picks its ARIA role from severity — a destructive alert interrupts, the rest wait their turn.

items.name: anomaly-chart
items.title: Anomaly Chart
items.description: A metric against its expected range, with outliers marked. The band is the point — 400ms at 03:00 may be an incident while 400ms at peak is Tuesday.

items.name: api-keys
items.title: API Keys
items.description: Credentials, listed and revocable. A key is shown in full exactly once — after that only the prefix and last four, because a list that can reveal every key means a session holds every secret.

items.name: aspect-ratio
items.title: Aspect Ratio
items.description: Hold a box at a fixed ratio while its width is fluid. Modern CSS aspect-ratio, so no padding-top hack.

items.name: asset-grid
items.title: Asset Grid
items.description: A media library as a selectable grid, built on this kit’s Image so every tile gets a placeholder, a reserved box and a failure state. A broken asset stays in the grid — it is exactly the one someone came to find and replace.

items.name: attachment-preview
items.title: Attachment Preview
items.description: A file chip with an icon chosen from the MIME type. Never from the extension: a `.dat` that is really a PDF should show a PDF, and a `.pdf` that is really an executable should not.

items.name: attribution
items.title: Attribution
items.description: Credit for a conversion split across touchpoints, with the model as a control rather than a buried setting — because the disagreement between models is the whole finding.

items.name: audio-player
items.title: Audio Player
items.description: A player built on the real <audio> element, so buffering, codecs, media keys, the OS lock screen and Bluetooth controls all keep working. State is read back off the element rather than mirrored, so anything else touching playback stays in sync.

items.name: audit-log
items.title: Audit Log
items.description: Who did what to which thing, when. Denied and errored attempts are kept and marked rather than filtered out — a log of successes only tells you nothing about the attack you are looking for.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: An image standing in for a person, with a fallback that always renders. Initials are derived from the name, and a broken image falls through to them.

items.name: back-to-top
items.title: Back To Top
items.description: Appears once you have scrolled, driven by an IntersectionObserver sentinel rather than a scroll handler — and it moves focus, not just the viewport.

items.name: backup-list
items.title: Backup List
items.description: Snapshots, and whether any of them would actually restore. A backup nobody has restored is a hypothesis, so an untested one is drawn as a warning rather than as a success.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A short status or category marker. Unlike a field, a badge exists to be noticed, so it keeps the full colour system and the tint escape hatch.

items.name: banner
items.title: Banner
items.description: A page-level announcement strip. Distinct from Alert, which belongs to the content around it — a banner spans the page and belongs to the session.

items.name: benchmark-table
items.title: Benchmark Table
items.description: Ranked results with variance. A difference inside the combined error bars is reported as "within noise" rather than as a win — printing "1.03× faster" from two noisy runs is how performance myths start.

items.name: bet-input
items.title: Bet Input
items.description: A stake field with quick multipliers and a live return. Stakes are integer minor units and the max is clamped to the balance, so "all in" cannot stake money that is not there.

items.name: blame-view
items.title: Blame View
items.description: Every line attributed to the commit that last touched it. Consecutive lines from one commit collapse into a single gutter entry — a blame view that repeats itself hides where one commit ends and the next begins.

items.name: bottom-nav
items.title: Bottom Nav
items.description: The mobile tab bar — three to five destinations, pinned to the bottom where thumbs are, with the home-indicator safe area accounted for.

items.name: box-plot
items.title: Box Plot
items.description: Quartiles, Tukey whiskers and outliers — the distribution an average hides. Quartiles use linear interpolation, so they agree with what your analytics stack reports.

items.name: branch-select
items.title: Branch Select
items.description: A branch and tag picker. A Combobox underneath — repositories routinely have hundreds of branches, so search is not optional — with the default branch pinned first and tags labelled.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: The trail back up the hierarchy. An ordered list in a labelled nav, with the current page marked aria-current and deliberately not linked.

items.name: bridge-status
items.title: Bridge Status
items.description: A cross-chain transfer as its two legs. Not one progress bar: the legs fail independently and the second cannot begin until the first is final, so a single bar implies a state that does not exist.

items.name: bucket-list
items.title: Bucket List
items.description: Object-storage buckets, with public access rendered as a warning rather than as one small grey tag among five. Every storage breach of the last decade is a bucket nobody realised was world-readable.

items.name: budget-guard
items.title: Budget Guard
items.description: Spend and token caps against what a run has consumed. A soft limit warns and a hard limit stops — collapsing them into one bar is how a team ends up believing they have a spend cap when what they have is a notification.

items.name: build-log
items.title: Build Log
items.description: Steps with their own output and timing bars. Failed steps open by default and successful ones stay closed — nobody opens a build log to read the steps that worked.

items.name: bulk-action-bar
items.title: Bulk Action Bar
items.description: The bar that appears once rows are selected. It states the count in words next to the destructive button, because "Delete" and "Delete 4,812 records" deserve different amounts of hesitation.

items.name: bundle-treemap
items.title: Bundle Treemap
items.description: Bundle size by module, laid out by compressed size. Raw bytes overstate text-heavy modules dramatically — a 400KB locale file that gzips to 12KB dominates a raw treemap and barely matters on the wire.

items.name: button-group
items.title: Button Group
items.description: Joins controls into one segmented unit — buttons, inputs, selects, or a mix. Inner corners are squared and adjacent borders overlap, so the row reads as a single control rather than a queue of separate ones.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: A control for a single action. Six variants across eight colour sets, ten sizes, and `asChild` to render as any element. Destructive is a colour, not a variant.

items.name: cache-stats
items.title: Cache Stats
items.description: Hit rate with the numbers behind it. 99% on 40 requests a day is noise and 80% on 4 million is a cost centre, so volume sits beside the percentage.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: A date grid in single or range mode, with presets, times, dropdown captions and multiple months. No date library — the grid, weekday names and times all come from Intl.

items.name: campaign-card
items.title: Campaign Card
items.description: An affiliate offer with its performance. EPC leads, not revenue — £40,000 and £4,000 cannot be ranked without knowing the traffic behind each, and earnings per click is the only comparable figure.

items.name: candlestick-chart
items.title: Candlestick Chart
items.description: OHLC candles with a volume strip. Unlike every other chart here it does not stretch — a stretched candle varies its body width with the container while the wick stays one unit, and the body-versus-wick reading stops working.

items.name: card-input
items.title: Card Input
items.description: Card number, expiry and CVC in one control, with brand detection and a Luhn check. Client-side validation catches the typo; it never claims the card is good.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: A surface that groups related content. Header and footer are optional and draw their own dividers — a Card holding only a CardBody is just a padded box.

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: A horizontally scrolling row of slides, built on CSS scroll-snap rather than a transform track — so touch swiping, momentum and keyboard scrolling all keep working.

items.name: cart
items.title: Cart
items.description: A basket with quantities and per-line totals. Stock limits are enforced at the stepper, not on submit — letting someone add a ninth of eight units and saying so at checkout is the worst possible order.

items.name: cascader
items.title: Cascader
items.description: A regular hierarchy picked one level at a time, in side-by-side columns — so the path stays readable and the siblings you passed are still visible.

items.name: chain-select
items.title: Chain Select
items.description: A network switcher. Testnets are labelled and grouped below mainnets — transacting on the wrong network is the most expensive user error in this space, and an unlabelled list invites it.

items.name: changelog-entry
items.title: Changelog Entry
items.description: A release grouped by change type, with breaking changes hoisted to the top whatever order they came in. Everything else in a changelog is optional reading; a breaking change is not.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: A small line, area or bar plot in plain SVG. Not a charting library — everything here is a scale and a path, which is the right trade for six numbers on a dashboard card.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: A binary choice. A real native checkbox under a styled box, so labels, forms, keyboard and the indeterminate state all work.

items.name: checkout-summary
items.title: Checkout Summary
items.description: The order total, broken into its lines. A charge that is not yet known renders as "calculated at next step" rather than as £0.00 — showing zero for a charge you will apply is a promise you cannot keep.

items.name: citations
items.title: Citations
items.description: Numbered sources for a generated answer. A marker is a real anchor with an accessible name, because a bare superscript "3" is meaningless read aloud — exactly when checking a claim matters most.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: Syntax-highlighted source with an optional title or file path, copy, inline editing, line numbers and collapsing.

items.name: code-search
items.title: Code Search
items.description: Search hits grouped by file, with the match marked inside its line. Ranges are clamped on render, because a wrong highlight is worse than none — it looks right.

items.name: cohort-table
items.title: Cohort Table
items.description: Retention by signup period, as a triangle. Cells are shaded by rate rather than by count, so a small cohort that retains well is not washed out by a large one that does not.

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.description: A single panel that expands and collapses. The open height is measured rather than assumed, because height: auto cannot be transitioned.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: Color Picker
items.description: A palette first, free entry second. Most product colour pickers choose a label or category colour, where an arbitrary hex is a liability — a gradient invites a colour nobody can read text on.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A Select you can type into. The search box lives inside the panel rather than replacing the trigger, so the chosen value stays visible while you filter.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: A command palette: type to filter, arrows to move, Enter to run. Items are data rather than children, because filtering has to reorder and hide them.

items.name: commit-graph
items.title: Commit Graph
items.description: The branch graph beside a commit list. Lanes are held by the commit each one is waiting for, which is what keeps a branch on a single vertical line instead of drifting sideways at every merge.

items.name: commit-list
items.title: Commit List
items.description: A history, grouped by day. The grouping is the point — a flat list of forty commits is unreadable, and "when" is the axis people actually scan along.

items.name: compare-slider
items.title: Compare Slider
items.description: Two images stacked, with a handle that wipes between them. Side-by-side thumbnails make the reader diff from memory; a wipe puts both states in the same pixels, so the difference is the only thing that moves.

items.name: composer
items.title: Composer
items.description: A live playground: drive a set of props and watch the generated source follow. Assembled from the kit’s own controls, so anything awkward about Select, Switch or NumberInput surfaces here first.

items.name: confidence-meter
items.title: Confidence Meter
items.description: How sure a model is, in five steps. Segmented on purpose — a smooth bar invites reading 0.834 as different from 0.851, which is not what a calibration score supports.

items.name: connection-pool
items.title: Connection Pool
items.description: What is checked out, idle and waiting. A pool at 100% with nothing queued is exactly the right size; the same pool with twelve waiting is an outage forming — so waiters are drawn beyond the bar rather than folded into it.

items.name: connection-string
items.title: Connection String
items.description: A DSN parsed into the parts that matter for its driver. A file-backed database has a path and no host, user or port — pretending every database is Postgres is what makes most of these components useless outside it.

items.name: container-list
items.title: Container List
items.description: Running containers with state, image tag and resource use. Restart count is shown whenever it is non-zero — a container "running" with 47 restarts is crash-looping, and its state says everything is fine.

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.description: A menu opened by right-click, positioned at the pointer. It has no element to anchor to — the anchor is a point — so it clamps against the viewport rather than flipping.

items.name: context-picker
items.title: Context Picker
items.description: Picks what an assistant can see. A dropdown rather than a dialog, because attaching context happens mid-thought and a modal takes focus off the prompt you were writing.

items.name: context-window
items.title: Context Window
items.description: What is in the context right now and how much room is left. Segments are drawn to scale against the window, not against what is used — a bar normalised to the used total always looks full, which is exactly backwards.

items.name: cookie-consent
items.title: Cookie Consent
items.description: A consent banner with reject as easy as accept, nothing pre-ticked, and no cookie written by the component itself — the arrangement regulators have repeatedly ruled is the compliant one.

items.name: coordinate-input
items.title: Coordinate Input
items.description: Latitude and longitude, accepting decimal degrees or DMS. A latitude above 90 is reported as "is this a longitude?" rather than "out of range" — swapped pairs are the most common coordinate bug there is.

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy Button
items.description: Copies a string and says so. Extracted after the same clipboard-plus-timer was written four times in this kit — CodeBlock, Terminal, EnvVars and Message all route through it now.

items.name: cost-breakdown
items.title: Cost Breakdown
items.description: Spend by model, with token volume beside it. The two routinely disagree — the cheap model handling 90% of calls is often 10% of the bill — and either number alone leads to the wrong optimisation.

items.name: countdown
items.title: Countdown
items.description: Time remaining until a deadline, ticking. It counts toward a Date rather than decrementing a number, because setInterval is throttled in a background tab — a decremented timer drifts and then confidently shows the wrong number.

items.name: coverage-report
items.title: Coverage Report
items.description: Coverage per file, ranked by uncovered lines rather than by percentage. A 400-line file at 92% has 32 untested lines; a 12-line file at 60% has 5 — and percentage ranks the small one first.

items.name: cron-schedule
items.title: Cron Schedule
items.description: Scheduled jobs: when each next runs and how the last went. An overdue job — next run in the past with nothing running — is called out, since that is the failure a schedule list exists to catch.

items.name: csv-preview
items.title: CSV Preview
items.description: A parsed CSV before you import it, showing the rows that will break the import. A preview that renders the first ten rows of a clean file has shown you nothing — mismatched column counts are what abort an import halfway.

items.name: curl-command
items.title: Curl Command
items.description: A request as a runnable curl command, shell-quoted and with secrets masked. This output gets pasted into tickets, and an Authorization header pasted into a ticket is a leaked credential.

items.name: currency-input
items.title: Currency Input
items.description: A money field whose value is an integer number of minor units, formatted only while unfocused. Reads its decimal count from Intl, so zero-decimal currencies work without a special case.

items.name: data-grid
items.title: Data Grid
items.description: Sorting and selection over Table, driven by a column definition. The sort is stable and never mutates your array, so re-sorting on an equal column leaves settled rows where they were.

items.name: data-quality
items.title: Data Quality
items.description: A column profile: how complete, how varied, and what the values look like. Sample values are the fastest way to spot that a “date” column holds three different formats — no summary statistic catches that.

items.name: date-picker
items.title: Date Picker
items.description: Calendar in a Popover with a trigger that reads like an Input. Every Calendar capability passes through — range, presets, times, multiple months — so there is one date implementation, not two.

items.name: date-range-compare
items.title: Date Range Compare
items.description: A metric against the same metric last period, with the basis named. "+18%" is meaningless until you know against what — and against a partial period it is meaningless full stop.

items.name: dependency-list
items.title: Dependency List
items.description: Packages with their update and vulnerability state. Severity outranks staleness in the sort, because ordering by how out of date things are buries a critical advisory behind forty patch bumps.

items.name: deploy-list
items.title: Deploy List
items.description: Deployments, newest first. A running deploy shows an indeterminate bar rather than a fabricated percentage — a number nobody can compute is worse than admitting you cannot.

items.name: description-list
items.title: Description List
items.description: Key/value metadata as a real <dl>, so a screen reader announces each term with its value. Columns on wide screens, stacked on narrow ones.

items.name: device-list
items.title: Device List
items.description: Devices trusted to skip the second factor, and when that trust lapses. A grant that expires in three days is worth seeing before you are asked for a code at an airport.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal window, built on the native <dialog> element — so the focus trap, background inerting, Escape handling and top-layer stacking come from the platform rather than from JavaScript.

items.name: diff-proposal
items.title: Diff Proposal
items.description: A model-proposed edit with accept and reject. The decision is reported, never applied — and once made, the actions are replaced by the outcome so a stale card cannot be clicked twice.

items.name: diff-stat
items.title: Diff Stat
items.description: Added and removed line counts with the five-square bar. The squares are proportional but never empty — one line changed in a thousand still lights one square.

items.name: diff-view
items.title: Diff View
items.description: A unified or side-by-side diff. Takes parsed hunks rather than a patch string, with parseUnifiedDiff exported alongside for when you only have the text.

items.name: donut
items.title: Donut
items.description: Parts against a whole. Arcs are stroke-dasharray on a circle rather than wedge paths — one number per slice, and no arc-flag branch at the halfway point.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description: A bottom sheet you can drag away. Built on a native dialog, so focus containment and inerting the page come from the platform rather than a hand-rolled trap.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown Menu
items.description: A menu of actions hung off a trigger. Unlike Select this is a list of commands, not a value — items are buttons, the menu closes on activation, and focus returns to the trigger.

items.name: dropzone
items.title: Dropzone
items.description: The upload card: click it or drag onto it, and it runs the upload. Hand it onUpload and it moves each file through queued, uploading, done or error, reports progress, and keeps failures on screen with a retry.

items.name: emoji-picker
items.title: Emoji Picker
items.description: A grouped, searchable grid with recents, rendered as text rather than sprites. One tab stop with arrow-key movement, and it never touches localStorage.

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: The state a list is in before it has anything in it. An icon, a reason and a next action are what make the empty case useful rather than merely honest.

items.name: endpoint-list
items.title: Endpoint List
items.description: API routes, grouped and filterable. The method badge is fixed-width because a route table is scanned down the method column, and a ragged left edge makes that scan impossible.

items.name: env-diff
items.title: Env Diff
items.description: Two environments side by side, values masked by default. A variable missing from one side is drawn differently from one whose value merely differs — "not set" and "set to something else" have different causes.

items.name: env-vars
items.title: Env Vars
items.description: Environment variables with secrets masked until asked for. Reveal is per-row and never sticky — nothing survives a remount, so a shared screen cannot leak what someone expanded an hour ago.

items.name: error-boundary
items.title: Error Boundary
items.description: Catches a render error in its subtree and shows a fallback. The one component here that must be a class — getDerivedStateFromError has no hook equivalent.

items.name: eval-board
items.title: Eval Board
items.description: Which model to ship, and what is still broken — as a ranking plus a case list rather than a grid. Chips carry their own model name, so there is no column header to align to and nothing that scrolls sideways at four models.

items.name: eval-results
items.title: Eval Results
items.description: A model-versus-benchmark score matrix. The best result is marked per benchmark rather than overall — a model can lead on reasoning and trail on latency, and one winner badge hides that.

items.name: event-stream
items.title: Event Stream
items.description: A live tail of analytics events with their payloads — the tool for debugging the tracking itself. Autoscroll pauses when you scroll away and the list is capped rather than unbounded.

items.name: feature-flag
items.title: Feature Flag
items.description: A flag with its rollout percentage and targeting rules. The kill switch is a separate control from the rollout — during an incident, turning it off must be one action, not a slider drag.

items.name: feedback
items.title: Feedback
items.description: Thumbs up or down, with an optional reason. The rating sends on click and the comment is a separate follow-up — holding the rating hostage to a comment box is how feedback widgets collect nothing.

items.name: few-shot-editor
items.title: Few-Shot Editor
items.description: The worked examples in a prompt, as editable pairs rather than one long string. Structured pairs can be counted, reordered, costed and switched off one at a time — a textarea holding six examples supports none of that.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: Wires a label, a control, help text and an error message together — id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid, all of which are easy to get one short of by hand.

items.name: file-preview
items.title: File Preview
items.description: One file rendered as whatever it actually is — image, text, audio, or an honest “no preview” panel. The MIME type decides, never the extension: a .png served as text/html is the oldest upload attack there is.

items.name: file-tree
items.title: File Tree
items.description: Files and directories as a tree. Uses the ARIA tree pattern with roving focus — arrow keys move between rows, so a repository with 200 files does not cost 200 tab stops.

items.name: fingerprint-diff
items.title: Fingerprint Diff
items.description: Two device fingerprints, with only the differing attributes shown. The question is never what a device looks like — it is what changed between two sessions, and twenty-eight matching rows hide the two that matter.

items.name: flame-graph
items.title: Flame Graph
items.description: Width is time, depth is stack. Frames stay in call order rather than being sorted by cost — reordering them destroys the shape a flame graph exists to show.

items.name: fmt
items.title: Fmt
items.description: One component for every formatted value — dates, numbers, currency, bytes, durations, relative times — so the locale is a single decision rather than three developers reaching for toLocaleString, toFixed and padStart on one screen.

items.name: form
items.title: Form
items.description: A thin bridge between React Hook Form and Field. Field owns the accessibility wiring and knows nothing about any form library; this adds only state and validation.

items.name: fraud-verdict
items.title: Fraud Verdict
items.description: The decision at the end of a review: what was decided, on what basis, by whom. A settled verdict offers to reopen rather than accept a second one, because two conflicting verdicts on one case is the failure this shape prevents.

items.name: funnel
items.title: Funnel
items.description: Conversion through ordered stages, with both the overall rate and the step rate. A funnel showing only the overall rate hides which single step is losing people.

items.name: gantt
items.title: Gantt
items.description: Work on a timeline: drag a bar to reschedule and its edges to change the start or end, with a computed critical path and dependency conflicts surfaced as you create them.

items.name: gas-tracker
items.title: Gas Tracker
items.description: Gas tiers with what each actually costs. Gwei alone is not a decision — the same gas price costs four times more for a swap than a transfer, which is why gasLimit is a prop.

items.name: gauge
items.title: Gauge
items.description: A radial meter — the circular counterpart to Progress. Drawn with stroke-dasharray rather than an arc path, so the sweep is one number and there is no arc-flag maths to get wrong.

items.name: governance-proposal
items.title: Governance Proposal
items.description: A proposal with its tally. Quorum is tracked separately from the majority because they are separate tests — a 92% "for" reads as passing right up until it fails for turnout.

items.name: group
items.title: Group
items.description: A recessed container that holds a set of cards. Padding and gap are the same value, and the corner radius is concentric with the cards inside it.

items.name: guardrail-list
items.title: Guardrail List
items.description: The safety checks around a run and how each one landed, ordered by consequence rather than by execution. A skipped check is its own state — “we did not scan” and “the scan found nothing” are opposite facts.

items.name: handoff-trail
items.title: Handoff Trail
items.description: Who handled a request, in order, and why each handover happened. The hardest question in a multi-agent system is “why did this agent answer”, and the answer is never in one agent’s transcript — it is in the chain.

items.name: health-checks
items.title: Health Checks
items.description: Endpoint probes with status, latency and history. A 200 that takes four seconds reads as degraded — a probe list that only reports the status code is why slow outages get noticed by customers first.

items.name: heatmap-grid
items.title: Heatmap Grid
items.description: A calendar heatmap — weeks as columns, weekdays as rows. UptimeStrip is the one-dimensional case; this is the grid.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: A preview card shown on hover — richer than a tooltip, and pointer-only. There is a close delay as well as an open delay, so the pointer can travel into the card without it vanishing.

items.name: http-status
items.title: HTTP Status
items.description: A status code with its reason phrase. Colour follows the class, never the individual code — grading a 503 as worse than a 500 invents a severity ordering that does not exist.

items.name: image-cropper
items.title: Image Cropper
items.description: The step between picking an image and saving it. The crop is stored in natural image coordinates and exported with toBlob, so it survives a resize and uploads directly.

items.name: image
items.title: Image
items.description: An img that reserves its space, covers its own load with a skeleton, shimmer or blurred thumbnail, builds a srcset from a list of widths, and renders a fallback in the same box when the URL is dead.

items.name: incident-card
items.title: Incident Card
items.description: An incident: severity, state, owner, age. Severity is a left edge rather than a tinted surface, because a list of ten red cards is unreadable and the stripe scales to a queue.

items.name: index-list
items.title: Index List
items.description: The indexes on a table and which are dead weight. An unused index is written on every insert and makes the planner’s job harder — but a primary key with no scans is not flagged, because suggesting you drop one is advice that loses data.

items.name: input-file
items.title: Input File
items.description: A file picker shaped like an Input that also runs the upload. Hand it onUpload and it moves each file through queued, uploading, done or error, reports progress, and keeps failures on screen with a retry.

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input OTP
items.description: A fixed-length code entry, one box per character. Every box is a real input so autofill can target it, and paste is distributed across all of them.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: A single-line text field, built on the headless Field primitive. Monochrome by design — it shares the Button size steps but none of its colour sets.

items.name: inspector
items.title: Inspector
items.description: The properties panel for whatever is selected — the other half of a canvas. Driven by a field schema rather than by children, because the fields change with the selection and writing that as JSX means a switch statement per kind at the call site.

items.name: invoice-list
items.title: Invoice List
items.description: Billing history. Amounts are right-aligned and tabular, which is the whole reason this is not a generic list — a money column that does not line up cannot be scanned.

items.name: ip-cluster
items.title: IP Cluster
items.description: Accounts grouped by a shared address or device. The shape is the finding: one node fanning out to eight accounts is multi-accounting, eight accounts each on their own address is a shared ISP.

items.name: json-viewer
items.title: JSON Viewer
items.description: A collapsible view of a parsed value. Collapsed nodes show their size, because "three entries or three thousand" is the question you have before expanding one.

items.name: jwt-inspector
items.title: JWT Inspector
items.description: Decodes a token into header, payload and signature. Decoding is not verification and the component says so — a green tick without the signing key would be actively dangerous.

items.name: kanban
items.title: Kanban
items.description: Columns of cards, movable between them. Drag-and-drop is pointer-only, so every card also moves with the arrow keys — a board you can only drag excludes keyboard users from its main action.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A keyboard key. Splits on "+" so a chord can be written as one string.

items.name: knowledge-graph
items.title: Knowledge Graph
items.description: Entities and the named relations between them. Where a note graph answers what is connected, this answers how — and the edge label carries as much meaning as the nodes, so relations are labelled and directed.

items.name: label-picker
items.title: Label Picker
items.description: Coloured repository labels, picked from a searchable list. Chip text is derived from the fill by luminance, since a label set imported from a forge only gives you a background colour.

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: A form label. htmlFor is the point — clicking it focuses the control, and a screen reader announces the two together.

items.name: leaderboard
items.title: Leaderboard
items.description: Ranked scores with movement since the last period, and the current user pinned even when they are nowhere near the top. A board you cannot find yourself on is a board you stop opening.

items.name: ledger-table
items.title: Ledger Table
items.description: Double-entry lines with a running balance. Debits and credits get their own columns and are totalled separately, because a ledger where the two do not agree is the finding.

items.name: lighthouse-score
items.title: Lighthouse Score
items.description: Category rings with the metrics behind them. A performance score of 62 is not actionable; "LCP 4.1s" is — so the metrics are shown, not hidden behind the summary.

items.name: liquidity-position
items.title: Liquidity Position
items.description: A concentrated-liquidity position with its range. In-range versus out-of-range is the headline — a position outside its range earns nothing, and a card showing only "fees earned" while it stopped earning last week is misleading.

items.name: live-announcer
items.title: Live Announcer
items.description: Imperative screen-reader announcements for things with no visible region of their own — a background save finishing, a filter narrowing a list.

items.name: location-picker
items.title: Location Picker
items.description: Pick a place by searching, or by typing coordinates. Both routes stay open: search covers the common case, the fields cover the field site or mooring that no geocoder knows.

items.name: log-viewer
items.title: Log Viewer
items.description: Structured logs with level filters, search and counts. Matches are highlighted in place rather than filtering the list down, so a search shows where the hits are in context.

items.name: login-form
items.title: Login Form
items.description: Email and password, with somewhere for SSO buttons and an error. The error is announced, not just coloured — a failed sign-in that only turns red is invisible to a screen reader.

items.name: map-embed
items.title: Map Embed
items.description: A map on CARTO's near-monochrome basemap. A full-colour street map fights everything drawn on top of it; a greyscale ground lets the marker be the only saturated thing on screen.

items.name: markdown-editor
items.title: Markdown Editor
items.description: A real textarea, a toolbar that edits the selection through setRangeText — so the browser undo stack survives — and the Markdown component as its preview.

items.name: markdown
items.title: Markdown
items.description: Rendered markdown with a switch to the source. It builds React nodes and never sets innerHTML, so a document you did not write cannot execute — and the RAW toggle is there because rendered output hides exactly what you look at when it renders wrongly.

items.name: market-table
items.title: Market Table
items.description: A market list with price, change, volume and cap. Rank is the caller’s, never the row index — a re-sorted table that renumbers from one destroys the identifier people use to talk about a market.

items.name: mask-input
items.title: Mask Input
items.description: Formats as you type — card numbers, phone numbers, dates. Hands back the raw characters alongside the formatted text, so a form does not submit "(555) 010-9999" to an API expecting digits.

items.name: masonry
items.title: Masonry
items.description: A column layout for items of unequal height, built on CSS columns rather than a JS layout pass — so it packs before paint and reflows on resize for free. Items order top-to-bottom within a column, which is the trade.

items.name: mcp-capability-matrix
items.title: MCP Capability Matrix
items.description: Which server provides which capability, and where two of them collide. MCP names are not namespaced by the protocol, so two servers exposing `search` is decided by your client’s merge order — silently. A per-server list can never show that.

items.name: mcp-config-editor
items.title: MCP Config Editor
items.description: The mcpServers config with the mistakes people actually make called out. The usual failure parses cleanly and the server silently never appears — the error is in the shape, not the syntax, so a JSON editor catches none of it.

items.name: mcp-elicitation
items.title: MCP Elicitation
items.description: A server asking the user for structured input mid-run. Useful, and a good phishing surface — the prompt text is written by the server and appears wearing your client’s chrome, so the requesting server is named outside its own copy.

items.name: mcp-prompt-list
items.title: MCP Prompt List
items.description: The prompts a server offers, with the arguments each one takes. How much has to be filled in is visible without expanding, because that is what decides which prompt you pick.

items.name: mcp-resource-list
items.title: MCP Resource List
items.description: The resources a server exposes, addressed by URI. The URI is always shown in full and is what search matches first — “SSH key” and file:///Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa are the same resource, and only one of them makes anyone look twice.

items.name: mcp-roots
items.title: MCP Roots
items.description: The roots a client has granted its servers — the closest thing MCP has to a permission boundary, and invisible in most clients. A root covering a whole home directory is drawn as a warning rather than as another grey row.

items.name: mcp-sampling
items.title: MCP Sampling
items.description: A server asking the client to run a model on its behalf. Sampling inverts the usual direction — the server sends the request, your model and your budget answer it — so the messages are shown verbatim before the buttons.

items.name: mcp-server-card
items.title: MCP Server Card
items.description: One MCP server: what it is, how it is attached, and what it brought with it. Leads with the transport and the actual command line, because a server named “filesystem” tells you nothing and `--root /` tells you everything.

items.name: mcp-server-picker
items.title: MCP Server Picker
items.description: A catalogue of servers you could install. Installing one is running someone else’s code with your credentials, so the card leads with publisher and verification rather than with the blurb — which is written by the person asking to be trusted.

items.name: media-gallery
items.title: Media Gallery
items.description: A grid that opens into a lightbox. `alt` is required by the type rather than optional, because a gallery is exactly where missing alt text accumulates.

items.name: mention-input
items.title: Mention Input
items.description: A textarea with @-mention autocomplete. The trigger only fires at a word boundary, so an email address does not open the menu halfway through every address anyone types.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description: An application menu bar. What makes it a menu bar rather than a row of dropdowns: once one menu is open, moving along the bar opens the next instead of merely focusing it.

items.name: merge-conflict
items.title: Merge Conflict
items.description: Both sides of a conflict with a resolution per hunk. "Keep both" is offered because it is frequently right — two people adding a different import conflict textually and agree semantically.

items.name: message
items.title: Message
items.description: One turn in a conversation. The two roles are shaped differently on purpose — a user message is a bubble, an assistant message is full-width prose, because a long answer in a bubble is unreadable.

items.name: migration-list
items.title: Migration List
items.description: Applied and pending migrations, sorted by version. A migration applied after a later version is flagged — that is the signature of two branches merged without a rebase, and it means this schema matches no single branch.

items.name: mint-panel
items.title: Mint Panel
items.description: Supply, price and quantity, with the total shown before the button. A price of "0.08 ETH" beside a quantity of 5 is not a number anyone should be multiplying in their head at a mint.

items.name: model-comparison
items.title: Model Comparison
items.description: Two or more outputs side by side with a pick. Columns are equal width and height regardless of content, because a taller box reads as the better answer before a word of it is read.

items.name: model-select
items.title: Model Select
items.description: Picks which model answers. A Select with the naming convention folded in, so "Opus · most capable" is scannable where a bare model id is not.

items.name: moderation-queue
items.title: Moderation Queue
items.description: Reported content with its report reasons and a decision. Sensitive items are blurred until revealed, because a moderator should choose when to look at the worst thing in the queue.

items.name: money-input
items.title: Money Input
items.description: A currency field that reads and writes integer minor units. Money that has been through a float has already lost — the value that leaves this control is a whole number of cents.

items.name: multi-select
items.title: Multi Select
items.description: Pick several options. The gap Select cannot fill — it is a single-value combobox by construction, which is why the LogViewer level filter had to become a threshold instead of a set.

items.name: multiplier-chart
items.title: Multiplier Chart
items.description: The rising curve of a crash-style round. The crash is a state, not an animation that ends — the frozen curve and the final figure stay on screen so a player who looked away still sees what happened.

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation Menu
items.description: A site nav bar with mega-menu panels and hover intent — a short open delay so crossing the bar does not flash panels, and a longer close delay so the panel is reachable.

items.name: network-status
items.title: Network Status
items.description: RPC health: block height, latency, sync state. Staleness is derived from the age of the last block — a stuck node answers cheerfully with an old height, so "connected" from the node proves nothing.

items.name: nft-card
items.title: NFT Card
items.description: A token tile: media, collection, price. Broken media resolves to a placeholder rather than collapsing the tile — IPFS gateways fail constantly and a grid that reflows on every 404 is unusable.

items.name: node-canvas
items.title: Node Canvas
items.description: A pannable, zoomable canvas of draggable nodes and the edges between them — the substrate for an agent pipeline, a retrieval chain or a build DAG. Nodes are real DOM, so you put your own components inside them.

items.name: note-graph
items.title: Note Graph
items.description: A vault of linked notes laid out by force — the Obsidian-shaped view. Nodes are sized by how many links touch them, hovering dims everything outside the neighbourhood, and orphans are drawn hollow rather than hidden.

items.name: notification-inbox
items.title: Notification Inbox
items.description: A notification list grouped by day, with unread state. Unread is reported, never assumed — a panel that marks everything read on render clears what the user never saw.

items.name: number-input
items.title: Number Input
items.description: A number field with steppers. Uses type="text" with inputMode="decimal", because the native number input silently discards what it cannot parse — a half-typed "1e" or "-" vanishes as you type it.

items.name: object-list
items.title: Object List
items.description: Objects in a bucket, with the prefix hierarchy object stores only pretend to have. There are no folders in S3-shaped storage — `a/b/c.png` is one flat key — so keys deeper than the current prefix collapse into a prefix row with a count.

items.name: odds-display
items.title: Odds Display
items.description: A selectable price in decimal, fractional or American. Decimal is the source of truth and the others are derived, so a format switch can never change what the bet actually pays.

items.name: on-call-schedule
items.title: On-call Schedule
items.description: A rotation across a window of days. Shifts are positioned proportionally rather than snapped to a day grid — rotations hand over at 09:00, and rounding shows the wrong person on call for most of two days.

items.name: order-book
items.title: Order Book
items.description: Bids and asks with cumulative depth. The bar is the running total from the top of book, not the size at that level — what matters when taking liquidity is how much sits between you and a price.

items.name: org-chart
items.title: Org Chart
items.description: A reporting hierarchy drawn top-down with connectors, built from flat { id, managerId } rows. Orphans and multiple roots are rendered rather than dropped; cycles are reported.

items.name: page-header
items.title: Page Header
items.description: The masthead a page opens with: eyebrow, title, lead and a meta row. Extracted after four pages in this catalogue had each grown their own copy and drifted apart.

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: Move between pages of results. The windowing rule — how many neighbours to show and where the gaps fall — is exported as pageItems, so it can be reused or tested on its own.

items.name: password-input
items.title: Password Input
items.description: A password field with a reveal toggle and an optional strength meter that rewards length over symbols — the thing naive meters get wrong when they demand punctuation from a passphrase.

items.name: payment-method
items.title: Payment Method
items.description: Saved cards and accounts, with expiry warnings. A card expiring next month is the reason a subscription fails, and saying so before it does is the entire value of this list.

items.name: payout-status
items.title: Payout Status
items.description: Where a payout is and when the money lands. "Expected Thursday" is the thing people open this to find out; the status word alone never answers it.

items.name: pdf-viewer
items.title: PDF Viewer
items.description: A PDF in the browser’s own viewer with a toolbar around it. It delegates the rendering on purpose, and always shows a download link — because embedded PDFs fail routinely.

items.name: permission-matrix
items.title: Permission Matrix
items.description: Roles against permissions, in a grid. Inherited grants are drawn differently from direct ones, because "why can this role still delete things" is the question a flat list of ticks cannot answer.

items.name: phone-input
items.title: Phone Input
items.description: A country selector and a national number that together produce E.164 — the shape every telephony API wants. Honest about not being a validator.

items.name: pipeline
items.title: Pipeline
items.description: CI stages left to right with parallel jobs stacked inside each. A stage is as bad as its worst job, so its state is derived rather than being another field to keep in sync.

items.name: popconfirm
items.title: Popconfirm
items.description: A confirmation anchored to the control that triggered it, for reversible or single-item actions — so the row you are asking about stays visible.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: Rich content anchored to a trigger. Positioned with a fixed-position popper that flips when it would overflow, and dismissed by Escape or an outside press.

items.name: port-table
items.title: Port Table
items.description: Published ports with their bind address. `0.0.0.0:5432` and `127.0.0.1:5432` are the difference between a database on the internet and a database on the machine — printing only the number hides that.

items.name: portfolio-balance
items.title: Portfolio Balance
items.description: Total value with its allocation. The hide toggle is part of the component, not an app-level bolt-on — people check balances on trains. Allocation is computed from the values, never taken as a percentage prop.

items.name: postback-config
items.title: Postback Config
items.description: A server-to-server postback URL, validated against its macros. A postback missing {click_id} returns 200 and attributes nothing — this says so before it ships rather than in a reconciliation weeks later.

items.name: presence
items.title: Presence
items.description: Who else is here. The overflow count carries its own tooltip listing the rest — a "+5" that cannot tell you who is unhelpful in exactly the moment you care.

items.name: price-ticker
items.title: Price Ticker
items.description: A live price with its change. The flash on update is colour only — a ticker that moves makes the whole page twitch — and it compares against the previous rendered price, not the day’s direction.

items.name: pricing-table
items.title: Pricing Table
items.description: Plans side by side. Every plan lists every feature, including the ones it lacks — omitting them makes the columns uneven and quietly hides what you would give up.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: How far along a task is. Omit the value for an indeterminate bar, which sweeps rather than fills — the one honest way to say "working, duration unknown".

items.name: prompt-diff
items.title: Prompt Diff
items.description: Two versions of a prompt with what changed between them. Prompts are the source code of an agent and almost never treated that way — the reason a run regressed is usually a sentence somebody rewrote three days ago.

items.name: prompt-input
items.title: Prompt Input
items.description: The composer for a chat: a growing textarea, attached context as removable chips, and a toolbar. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a newline, and IME composition is checked first.

items.name: prompt-template
items.title: Prompt Template
items.description: A prompt with {{variable}} placeholders and a form to fill them. Variables are parsed out of the template rather than declared separately, so the two cannot drift.

items.name: prompt-variables
items.title: Prompt Variables
items.description: A prompt template with its slots filled in, beside the exact text the model receives. Variables are parsed out of the template rather than declared separately, so they cannot drift out of sync with it.

items.name: prompt-versions
items.title: Prompt Versions
items.description: A prompt’s history with what each change did to the score. The pairing is the point: a history without outcomes says what happened, a score chart without edits says something changed, and neither answers which edit made it worse.

items.name: pull-request-card
items.title: Pull Request Card
items.description: A pull request at a glance — state, branches, checks, reviewers. State is shown as an icon and a word, never colour alone.

items.name: qr-code
items.title: QR Code
items.description: A QR code encoded in the browser and drawn as SVG. No dependency and no network round trip — which matters, because the two things people encode most are a TOTP secret and a wallet address.

items.name: query-constructor
items.title: Query Constructor
items.description: A SELECT assembled a clause at a time — sources with a join button, columns, filter, then order, group and limit — with the finished statement underneath. Reads both ways: paste a SELECT and the blocks fill in. Values compile to bound parameters and identifiers are allow-listed against the schema.

items.name: query-editor
items.title: Query Editor
items.description: A SQL editor that asks before running an UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE clause. That is the most expensive mistake anyone makes in a query console, and it is trivial to detect.

items.name: query-plan
items.title: Query Plan
items.description: An EXPLAIN tree with cost bars drawn from self cost, not total. Every root holds 100% of total by definition, so a total-cost bar makes the root look like the problem in every query ever profiled.

items.name: queue-monitor
items.title: Queue Monitor
items.description: Depth, throughput and whether the queue is keeping up. Depth alone says nothing — 40,000 draining at 5,000/s is fine, 300 draining at 2/s is an incident.

items.name: radar-chart
items.title: Radar Chart
items.description: Several measures for one subject on axes radiating from a centre. Good for recognising a profile’s shape; documented plainly as the wrong chart when the reader needs to compare values.

items.name: radio-group
items.title: Radio Group
items.description: One choice out of several. Built on native radio inputs, so arrow-key roving, form submission and the single-selection invariant come from the platform.

items.name: range-slider
items.title: Range Slider
items.description: Two thumbs over one track. Slider is a restyled native input[type=range], which has exactly one thumb by construction — so a range needs a custom control with the ARIA written out.

items.name: rate-limit-meter
items.title: Rate Limit Meter
items.description: A quota with its reset time given equal weight. "9,800 of 10,000" is alarming; "resets in 40 seconds" makes it fine — showing the first without the second sends people to build a cache they do not need.

items.name: rating
items.title: Rating
items.description: A rating, readable or settable, drawn with monochrome marks. The icon is a prop; read-only renders one image with a text alternative — "4 out of 5" — rather than five separate announcements.

items.name: reasoning-block
items.title: Reasoning Block
items.description: A model's intermediate reasoning, folded away by default — it is supporting evidence, not the answer, and a panel that opens itself pushes the answer below the fold.

items.name: regex-tester
items.title: Regex Tester
items.description: A pattern against a test string, with matches highlighted and capture groups listed. Zero-length matches are guarded — `/a*/g` matches empty at every position and hangs a naive exec loop.

items.name: release-list
items.title: Release List
items.description: A changelog as a document — each version an article with a real heading, so it can be linked to and navigated by heading. Never sorts, since "newest first" cannot be derived from semver once pre-releases exist.

items.name: replication-status
items.title: Replication Status
items.description: A primary and its replicas with how far behind each one is, in seconds and bytes. Seconds say how stale a read is; bytes say whether it is catching up or falling further behind — a replica idling on 200MB of unsent log shows 0s until traffic arrives.

items.name: request-builder
items.title: Request Builder
items.description: Method, URL, headers, query and body. Query parameters are edited as rows and the assembled URL is shown beneath — hand-editing a query string is where encoding bugs come from.

items.name: resizable
items.title: Resizable
items.description: Two panels with a draggable divider. Sizes are percentages, so the split survives a container resize — and the handle is a real slider, so arrow keys resize it too.

items.name: resource-meter
items.title: Resource Meter
items.description: Used against a cap: build minutes, storage, seats, rate limits. Unlike Progress it can exceed 100%, because a quota can be 130% used and hiding that is how a bill becomes a surprise.

items.name: response-viewer
items.title: Response Viewer
items.description: Status, timing, size, headers and body. The three headline figures share one line because they are read together — a 200 that took 4 seconds is a different result from one that took 40ms.

items.name: result
items.title: Result
items.description: The whole-page outcome — not found, forbidden, server error, done. Announced on render, so a client-side route change to an error page is not silent for a screen reader.

items.name: retention-curve
items.title: Retention Curve
items.description: What fraction of each cohort is still here, period by period — normalised so growth cannot hide churn. Later cohorts are drawn shorter, not padded with zeroes.

items.name: retrieval-results
items.title: Retrieval Results
items.description: The chunks a retrieval step pulled, with relevance. Near-misses are dimmed rather than dropped — when an answer is wrong, "what did it nearly retrieve" is the useful question.

items.name: retry-policy
items.title: Retry Policy
items.description: A retry policy and the attempts it produced. A policy shown alone reads as reasonable right up until you see it fired four times in ninety milliseconds — the attempt list is what proves the policy running is the one configured.

items.name: revenue-share-table
items.title: Revenue Share Table
items.description: How a payout splits between parties. The unallocated remainder gets a named row instead of leaving the reader to subtract, and a split exceeding 100% is called out rather than quietly rendered.

items.name: review-thread
items.title: Review Thread
items.description: A review conversation anchored to a line of code, with the line shown as context. Resolving is always a callback — a resolved thread is server truth other reviewers see.

items.name: risk-score
items.title: Risk Score
items.description: A score with the signals that produced it. The factors are the component, not a detail beside it — an analyst cannot approve or decline on "82", and an unexplained score is the one thing a regulator will ask you to justify.

items.name: root-cause-tree
items.title: Root Cause Tree
items.description: A causal chain from symptom to candidate causes, each with a confidence band. Built on Tree, so it inherits the keyboard model rather than growing a second one.

items.name: round-history
items.title: Round History
items.description: Recent results as a strip. It carries an explicit note that past rounds do not predict the next one, because a row of results is read as a pattern whether or not one exists.

items.name: rpc-console
items.title: RPC Console
items.description: The JSON-RPC wire between a client and an MCP server. Requests and responses are paired by id, which is what produces the latency figure and what makes an unanswered request visible — the single most useful thing this view can show.

items.name: run-controls
items.title: Run Controls
items.description: The transport bar for an agent run: start, pause, step, stop, replay. Which buttons exist is derived from status, so the invalid combinations — running and paused, replay while live — cannot be expressed.

items.name: runbook-steps
items.title: Runbook Steps
items.description: Remediation steps, run one at a time and only in order. Offering "run" on step four while step two is untried invites exactly the mistake the runbook exists to prevent.

items.name: sandbox-policy
items.title: Sandbox Policy
items.description: The permissions an agent actually runs under — filesystem, network and process execution. Built to make the dangerous configuration look dangerous: an allow-list of `/` is functionally no sandbox, and it says so.

items.name: sankey
items.title: Sankey
items.description: Flow between stages, where band width is the quantity moving. Nodes are layered by longest path so every link runs forward, and a cycle is reported rather than drawn as something plausible.

items.name: scatter-plot
items.title: Scatter Plot
items.description: Two measured variables plotted against each other, with an optional least-squares trend line and Pearson’s r. Points can carry a third dimension as area and a fourth as colour.

items.name: scheduler
items.title: Scheduler
items.description: A week of days with events laid out against the hours and edited in place — drag to move across days, drag an edge to change the end, drag empty grid to create. Overlaps split into columns rather than stacking.

items.name: schema-form
items.title: Schema Form
items.description: A form generated from a JSON Schema, so a person can invoke a tool by hand. The counterpart to Tool Schema: that one explains the parameters, this one collects them — together they are how you test an MCP tool without writing a client.

items.name: schema-table
items.title: Schema Table
items.description: Columns, keys and indexes. Foreign keys name their target inline, because `owner_id` tells you nothing about whether it points at users or accounts — which is exactly what you opened the schema to find out.

items.name: schema-viewer
items.title: Schema Viewer
items.description: JSON Schema as a tree. Required fields are marked on the field itself rather than left in the parent's `required` array — cross-referencing that list is the one job a renderer should do for you.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: Scroll Area
items.description: A scrollable region with a themed scrollbar, styled through the standard scrollbar properties rather than a JavaScript overlay — so native momentum and keyboard scrolling stay intact.

items.name: seed-phrase
items.title: Seed Phrase
items.description: A recovery phrase, blurred until revealed. Deliberately hostile to convenience: no copy button and no selection, because a seed phrase on the clipboard is readable by every page visited afterwards.

items.name: segment-builder
items.title: Segment Builder
items.description: Build an audience from conditions, with precedence shown as nesting rather than implied by a word — and the output a structure, not a concatenated string.

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented Control
items.description: A small set of mutually exclusive choices shown at once, built from real radio inputs in a fieldset — so arrow keys, form submission and screen-reader announcement all work without any script.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: A custom dropdown, not a native select — the trigger matches Input exactly and the panel is real markup. Full keyboard support, type-ahead, and dismissal on Escape or outside click.

items.name: separator
items.title: Separator
items.description: A rule between sections, horizontal or vertical, optionally with a label set into it.

items.name: service-status
items.title: Service Status
items.description: The rows of a status page. The headline banner is derived from the services — a status page whose headline can disagree with its own rows is worse than none.

items.name: session-list
items.title: Session List
items.description: Active sign-ins, with the current one pinned and unrevokable from here. Signing yourself out of the session you are using is a footgun, so it is simply not offered.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: A panel that slides in from an edge. Same native <dialog> machinery as Dialog, pinned to one side — so it inherits the focus trap and Escape handling.

items.name: shortcut-sheet
items.title: Shortcut Sheet
items.description: A keyboard reference grouped by area. Presentational by design — it never binds the keys, because the component that shows a cheat sheet is not the one that owns the handlers.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.description: An inset application frame: a transparent rail that collapses to a 52px icon strip, beside a rounded content panel. Inset is the only layout and icon is the only collapsed state, which is what keeps the geometry exact.

items.name: signature-pad
items.title: Signature Pad
items.description: A canvas you sign with a finger, stylus or mouse. Strokes are kept as points and redrawn, so undo, resize and export all work — and stylus pressure varies the line.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: A placeholder shape for content that has not arrived. The pulse animates opacity only, so it stays inside the kit motion rule, and stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: skip-link
items.title: Skip Link
items.description: The first tab stop: jump past the navigation to the content. Invisible until focused, which is the whole design.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: Pick a value along a range. A restyled native range input, so arrow keys, Home/End, touch dragging and form submission all work without JavaScript.

items.name: slo-budget
items.title: SLO Budget
items.description: An error budget and how fast it is burning. Shows the budget remaining rather than availability achieved — 99.4% against a 99.9% target sounds like a near miss and is a six-times overspend.

items.name: slow-query-log
items.title: Slow Query Log
items.description: The queries costing you the most, ranked by total time rather than mean. The 9-second report running twice a day is easy to find; the 40ms lookup running four thousand times a minute is the one saturating the database.

items.name: sparkline
items.title: Sparkline
items.description: A microchart with no axes, legend or dependency — plain SVG over a normalised range, sized by whatever box you put it in.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: An indeterminate busy indicator. Rotation is the one exception the motion rule has to allow — a still spinner says nothing. It stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: stack-trace
items.title: Stack Trace
items.description: A parsed exception with its frames. Library frames collapse behind a count — a stack is typically three frames of your code buried in forty of the framework’s.

items.name: staking-panel
items.title: Staking Panel
items.description: A staking position: stake, rewards, APY and unlock. APY is labelled variable unless told otherwise, because it almost always is — a bare percentage reads as a fixed-term rate.

items.name: stat
items.title: Stat
items.description: One measurement: label, value and how it moved. Which direction counts as healthy is a prop, because a rise in incidents is not a rise in deployments.

items.name: status-checks
items.title: Status Checks
items.description: The CI check list on a pull request. The summary states the blocking outcome rather than the raw tally, because "3 failing" says nothing about whether you can merge.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: Progress through a fixed sequence. One `current` index drives the common case; any step can override its own status for a failure or a skip in the middle.

items.name: storage-usage
items.title: Storage Usage
items.description: A quota and what is filling it. The bar is scaled to the quota, not to what is used, so free space reads as free space — a bar normalised to the total consumed is always full, which is backwards for a component answering “how much room is left”.

items.name: story
items.title: Story
items.description: A full-screen sequence of panels over a darkened page. A dialog underneath — same overlay, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock — but it advances on its own, and everything else follows from that.

items.name: stream-inspector
items.title: Stream Inspector
items.description: A model’s token stream event by event, with the timing between them. An average tokens-per-second hides both numbers that matter — time to first token, and the stalls after it.

items.name: streaming-text
items.title: Streaming Text
items.description: Text revealed as it arrives, with a caret while it is still coming. Driven by elapsed time rather than a per-character interval, so it never drifts or dumps a backlog after a background tab.

items.name: subagent-tree
items.title: Subagent Tree
items.description: The tree of subagents a run spawned and what each is costing. Cost aggregates up the tree — a parent that spent 400 tokens itself and fanned out to children that spent 90,000 is cheap by its own line and ruinous in total.

items.name: subscription-state
items.title: Subscription State
items.description: Plan, price and what happens next. A cancelled subscription with three weeks of access left is the case people most often get wrong, and a status badge alone never says it.

items.name: suggestions
items.title: Suggestions
items.description: Starter prompts, offered before the first message. Buttons rather than a list, because each one performs an action.

items.name: swap-panel
items.title: Swap Panel
items.description: The pay/receive form of a token swap. Price impact is surfaced rather than buried behind a details toggle, and above a threshold the action is disabled outright.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: An instant on/off toggle. A native checkbox with role="switch", so it submits with a form and toggles from the keyboard.

items.name: symbol-outline
items.title: Symbol Outline
items.description: A file's symbols as a tree, in file order rather than alphabetical. An outline is a map of the document you are reading; re-sorting it makes the outline and the editor disagree about where things are.

items.name: table-of-contents
items.title: Table of Contents
items.description: An anchor list that tracks which heading is on screen, through IntersectionObserver rather than scroll offsets. Reads the DOM by default, so it works for rendered markdown.

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.description: Rows and columns of structured data. The wrapper scrolls rather than the page, so a wide table never forces horizontal scroll on the whole document.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Switch between panels in the same context. Full WAI-ARIA keyboard support: arrows rove, Home and End jump, and only the active tab is in the tab order.

items.name: tag-input
items.title: Tag Input
items.description: Free-text chips for keywords, recipients or labels. Backspace on an empty field removes the last tag, and pasting a comma-separated list splits it rather than making one long tag.

items.name: terminal
items.title: Terminal
items.description: Console output with ANSI colour. Follow-tail sticks to the bottom only while the reader is already there, so scrolling up to read something is never undone by the next line.

items.name: test-results
items.title: Test Results
items.description: A test run with suites, tests and failure output. Failures expand by default and passes stay collapsed — nobody opens a report to read what passed.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: The multi-line sibling of Input. Same variants, same padding rule, with a resize control and no icon slot.

items.name: theme-toggle
items.title: Theme Toggle
items.description: Switches the document between light and dark. Uncontrolled by default: it reads the class already on the element rather than flashing to its own idea of the default on mount.

items.name: thread-list
items.title: Thread List
items.description: An inbox of conversations. Unread is carried by weight and a count, not by colour alone, and the timestamp coarsens with age — a message from March does not need a clock time.

items.name: ticket-card
items.title: Ticket Card
items.description: A support ticket with its SLA. Breach risk is computed from the due time, not from how old the ticket is — a two-week ticket with a monthly SLA is fine, and an hour-old one may not be.

items.name: time-picker
items.title: Time Picker
items.description: Pick a time of day from generated slots. The value is always HH:mm in 24-hour form regardless of how it is displayed — the format is presentation, the value is data.

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline
items.description: A vertical run of events sharing one rail — deploys, incidents, review activity, an agent run. The connector stops at the last item instead of dangling past it.

items.name: timezone-select
items.title: Timezone Select
items.description: An IANA timezone picker showing each zone's current offset and local time. Zones are named by city, never by abbreviation — "CST" is Central, China and Cuba Standard Time.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Transient messages that stack and dismiss themselves. A provider plus a useToast() hook rather than a global singleton, so the queue lives in React state and two regions can coexist.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: A button that stays pressed. Uses aria-pressed rather than a checkbox, because this is a control that changes state, not a value submitted with a form.

items.name: token-amount
items.title: Token Amount
items.description: A balance formatted from base units without ever touching a float. 1 ETH is 10¹⁸ wei, which exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER by two orders of magnitude — a balance that passes through a JavaScript number is silently wrong.

items.name: token-approvals
items.title: Token Approvals
items.description: Spending allowances granted to contracts, with revoke. An unlimited approval is stated as "unlimited" rather than rendered as 2²⁵⁶−1, which reads like a display bug — it is a standing permission to move the whole balance, forever.

items.name: token-inspector
items.title: Token Inspector
items.description: Text broken into tokens, so a prompt’s cost stops being a mystery number. Tokenisation is not words — `astralyx` is three tokens — and people shorten prose while a JSON blob below costs ten times more.

items.name: token-select
items.title: Token Select
items.description: A token picker with balances and search. Symbols are not unique — anyone can deploy a contract called "USDC" — so unverified tokens are segregated, badged, and shown by contract address rather than the name they claim.

items.name: token-usage
items.title: Token Usage
items.description: How much of a context window is spoken for. The colour crosses to amber at 75% and destructive at 90%, because the number only matters once it is close.

items.name: tool-approval
items.title: Tool Approval
items.description: The consent prompt before a tool runs. The arguments are shown in full above the buttons, because “Allow issue_refund?” asks you to approve a function name — what matters is that it wants to move £3,400.

items.name: tool-call
items.title: Tool Call
items.description: One tool invocation inside an assistant turn. Collapsed by default — the arguments are long and the interesting part is that it ran — except a failure, which opens itself.

items.name: tool-diff
items.title: Tool Diff
items.description: What changed in a tool’s contract between two server versions, with breaking changes classified rather than just listed. Adding an optional parameter and making one required are both edits to `properties`; only one breaks every existing call.

items.name: tool-latency
items.title: Tool Latency
items.description: Per-tool latency and failure rate — the ops view of a tool fleet. Bars are drawn from p95, not the mean: a tool averaging 200ms that spikes to nine seconds one call in twenty is the one blowing your timeout, and the mean hides it.

items.name: tool-picker
items.title: Tool Picker
items.description: The catalogue of tools an agent may call, with a switch on each. Destructive capabilities are marked rather than hidden — the whole risk of an agent is a capability nobody noticed it had.

items.name: tool-result
items.title: Tool Result
items.description: What a tool actually returned, rendered by content type. An MCP result is a list of blocks that can mix text, images and embedded resources — JSON.stringify turns a returned screenshot into four thousand characters of base64.

items.name: tool-schema
items.title: Tool Schema
items.description: A tool’s parameter schema, rendered as something a person can read. Required, type and default get their own column, because those are the three questions anyone actually has about a parameter.

items.name: toolbar
items.title: Toolbar
